text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ousted Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto said she would move the Supreme Court against her dismissal by the President Farooq Leghari and also called upon Leghari to resign to provide a level playing-field for everyone in the coming elections.
- Asif Zardari, spouse of former prime minietr, is in custody of a non-civilian intelligence agency, sources said.
- The International Monetary Fund has sought an assurance from the caretaker government that it will implement the agreement reached between the IMF and the ousted government in letter and spirit.
- The state's Central Board of Revenue has cleared all the oustanding claims of duty drawbacks to the tune of 70 billion rupees in the last 15 months.
- An Economic Cooperation Organisation official said ECO founder-members Turkey, Iran and Pakistan had agreed to give $100 million each in equity to the proposed ECO Trade and Development Bank.
- The caretaker cabinet in its first meeting approved many proposals for cutting down expenditure on the maintenance of the cabinet ministers.
- A three-member team led by Governor State (central) Bank of Pakistan Muhammad Yaqub has been set up to identify political appointments in the state-run banks and financial insitutions.

- Two senior officials of the World Bank, Shahid Javed Burki and Ishrat Hussain, are arriving in Islamabad on Friday from Washington for restructuring the economy of Pakistan and introducing tariff and other reforms, sources said.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange 100-share index rose 78.48 points -- the highest one-day since November 1991 when it rose 88 points in a single session.

Differences are said to have cropped up between President Leghari and caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid who refused to approach the Supreme Court to delay polls set for February 3, 1997, sources said.
- Three more ministers were inducted into the cabinet increasing its strength to 12.
